item.text: {"chapter_id":"8B","issues":[{"question_id":"8B.1","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0024-E001","BATCH-0024-E007","BATCH-0042-E009"],"explanation":"The answer treats 2018 program materials and a September 2022 fact-check as if they directly establish the 2023 frozen program; they are useful baselines but require explicit continuity and later confirmation."},{"question_id":"8B.1","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E003","BATCH-0016-E001","BATCH-0016-E002"],"explanation":"The claim that repeated choices revealed a stable priority of stronger executive influence over autonomous institutions is interpretive and is not directly established by the cited evidence alone."},{"question_id":"8B.2","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0044-E010","BATCH-0044-E011","BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0055-E003"],"explanation":"These citations establish decrees, formal operating rules, and safeguards, but not that the administration actually translated them into executed compliance, functioning enforcement, or delivered capacity."},{"question_id":"8B.2","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-E001","BATCH-0049-E006","BATCH-0050-E005"],"explanation":"Several cited budget and program figures are 2022 or planned 2023 figures; the answer presents them collectively as evidence of 2023 operationalization without distinguishing approved inputs from executed action."},{"question_id":"8B.2","issue_type":"attribution_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0018-E015","BATCH-0018-E015"],"explanation":"Vacancies and appointments involved the Senate and other appointing institutions; the answer correctly qualifies this later but still frames the overall appointment record as presidential translation of the program."},{"question_id":"8B.3","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0047-E001","BATCH-0016-E007","BATCH-0055-E016"],"explanation":"Military expenditure, staffing, and training are given substantial positive weight even though the index explicitly says they are inputs and do not establish effective mobilization toward outcomes."},{"question_id":"8B.3","issue_type":"attribution_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0049-E006","BATCH-0054-E007","BATCH-0055-E016"],"explanation":"CONEVAL institutional performance and military training figures are attributed broadly to presidential mobilization, although the index identifies agency, legislative, or dissenting-opinion sources and does not establish personal presidential direction."},{"question_id":"8B.3","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0041-E003","BATCH-0048-E010","BATCH-0052-E004","BATCH-0052-E006"],"explanation":"The answer omits material evidence of weak controls, under-executed health investment, unclear program purposes, absent result measurement, and ignored monitoring recommendations that directly qualify claims of effective mobilization."},{"question_id":"8B.4","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0039-E001","BATCH-0055-E016"],"explanation":"A qualified Banxico appointment and military training numbers do not establish that the selected people were capable implementers of López Obrador's broader governing portfolio or that the president assessed and managed their performance."},{"question_id":"8B.4","issue_type":"irrelevant_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0002-E012"],"explanation":"The draft does not use these nuclear items here, but its personnel argument implicitly generalizes from technical institutional systems; those records concern CFE/CNSNS and lack presidential attribution, so they cannot support ruler-level appointment competence."},{"question_id":"8B.4","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0046-E008","BATCH-0026-E003","BATCH-0011-E001"],"explanation":"The answer mentions Segalmex reassignment but underweights the scale of documented procurement irregularities and the limited disciplinary response, which are decisive contrary evidence on retaining and replacing capable implementers."},{"question_id":"8B.5","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E007","BATCH-0052-E005","BATCH-0032-E006"],"explanation":"National reach, coverage, and target exceedance do not establish uniform territorial compliance, coordination, service quality, or milestone completion; the cited items expressly warn that coverage is not execution."},{"question_id":"8B.5","issue_type":"attribution_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E015","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0052-E005"],"explanation":"Otis coordination and social-program reach involved UN, civil-society, state, municipal, and other partners. The answer's positive coordination characterization risks crediting López Obrador for joint or externally supported activity."},{"question_id":"8B.5","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E004","BATCH-0052-E006","BATCH-0018-E006","BATCH-0018-E015"],"explanation":"The answer omits directly relevant evidence that programs lacked result orientation, ignored recommendations, had weak monitoring and payment systems, and that senior appointments remained unresolved."},{"question_id":"8B.6","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0030-E004","BATCH-0010-E009","BATCH-0029-E007"],"explanation":"Opening or constructing projects and assigning civilian functions to the military establish observable activity, but not successful enforcement, service quality, lawful completion, or achievement of the projects' stated objectives."},{"question_id":"8B.6","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E002","BATCH-0054-E007","BATCH-0015-E013","BATCH-0015-E016"],"explanation":"Monitoring outputs, UN program outputs, and institutional activities are weighted as evidence of broad implementation even though the index states they do not prove national incidence, enforcement, or policy impact."},{"question_id":"8B.6","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0041-E003","BATCH-0052-E004","BATCH-0052-E006","BATCH-0052-E005"],"explanation":"The answer does not include the strongest 2023 program-monitoring evidence: four priority programs did not measure results, logical linkages were often absent or weak, recommendations were disregarded, and two programs lacked coverage indicators."},{"question_id":"8B.7","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E002","BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0032-E009"],"explanation":"Most welfare outcomes cited are 2018-2022 results released in 2023, not outcomes observed during the full target year; the answer acknowledges this but still uses them as the principal 2023 result base."},{"question_id":"8B.7","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E006","BATCH-0031-E008","BATCH-0052-E014"],"explanation":"Expanded pension coverage, minimum wages, and 3.2% GDP growth show policy outputs or aggregate change, but do not by themselves demonstrate movement toward the ruler's full frozen portfolio or presidential causation."},{"question_id":"8B.7","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E002","BATCH-0031-E016","BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0032-E010"],"explanation":"The answer omits or underweights evidence of GDP-per-capita stagnation, increased health deprivation, higher catastrophic health spending, and reduced public healthcare use, all central adverse outcomes for the stated poverty, welfare, and development program."},{"question_id":"8B.7","issue_type":"irrelevant_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E014"],"explanation":"Aggregate 2023 GDP growth is only weakly relevant to ruler effectiveness without a clearly identified growth goal, baseline, counterfactual, and attribution analysis; the cited World Bank item itself emphasizes external and structural causes."},{"question_id":"8B.8","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E003","BATCH-0004-E008","BATCH-0032-E003"],"explanation":"Creating commissions, changing health institutions, and revising disappearance-counting systems demonstrate institutional change, not that audits or failures caused presidential learning, method adaptation, or verified improvement."},{"question_id":"8B.8","issue_type":"irrelevant_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0002-E012"],"explanation":"Nuclear drills, peer review, and corrective actions are attributed to CFE/CNSNS and lack López Obrador attribution; they are therefore irrelevant to judging his adaptation unless tied to a presidential decision or governing priority."},{"question_id":"8B.8","issue_type":"attribution_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0054-E007","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0051-E005"],"explanation":"CONEVAL and IMSS formal evaluation systems show institutional monitoring capacity, not that López Obrador used findings to change policy. The answer notes this limitation but still treats the systems as positive adaptation evidence."},{"question_id":"8B.8","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E004","BATCH-0052-E006","BATCH-0052-E020","BATCH-0054-E005"],"explanation":"The answer omits direct evidence that recommendations were disregarded, results orientation deteriorated in some programs, World Bank projects were cancelled or restructured amid policy shifts, and over half of monitored indicators were insufficient or lagging."},{"question_id":"8B.9","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E004","BATCH-0010-E002","BATCH-0029-E007"],"explanation":"Decisive presidential choices and military deployment are treated as evidence of crisis-management effectiveness, although the cited records establish control or response activity rather than preservation or advancement of the ruler's objectives."},{"question_id":"8B.9","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0031-E003","BATCH-0050-E010","BATCH-0049-E005","BATCH-0055-E006"],"explanation":"The answer mentions Otis delays and Ayotzinapa obstruction but does not fully integrate delayed aid, distribution failures, military-led nontransparent investigations, and the administration's continuation of invalidated military-control policy as failures of crisis and resistance management."},{"question_id":"8B.9","issue_type":"attribution_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E015","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0012-E014"],"explanation":"UN coordination and diplomatic positioning are presented as response evidence despite substantial partner involvement and no demonstrated influence over the crisis or international conflict."},{"question_id":"8B.10","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E006","BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0029-E007"],"explanation":"Expanded transfers, formal IMSS-BIENESTAR rules, and military administration show institutional or budgetary change, but not durable law, effective capacity, achieved outcomes, or post-period resilience."},{"question_id":"8B.10","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0030-E004","BATCH-0029-E007","BATCH-0052-E014"],"explanation":"The answer gives substantial positive weight to infrastructure and military apparatus despite evidence of incompleteness, cost escalation, uncertain benefits, and lack of demonstrated profitability or durable service outcomes."},{"question_id":"8B.10","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E002","BATCH-0016-E010","BATCH-0013-E010"],"explanation":"The answer incorporates retrospective and partly post-period assessments, including indicators extending into 2024 or using mixed reference years, without consistently separating evidence available by the end of 2023."},{"question_id":"8B.10","issue_type":"missing_contrary_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E004","BATCH-0052-E006","BATCH-0052-E015","BATCH-0052-E020"],"explanation":"The end-period synthesis omits major evidence of weak program logic, absent result measurement, World Bank objective failure, cancellations, institutional turnover, and policy discontinuity, all directly relevant to durability and fragility."},{"question_id":"8B.10","issue_type":"irrelevant_evidence","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E016","BATCH-0052-E014"],"explanation":"Fiscal restraint, macroeconomic stability, and 2023 GDP growth are treated as durable program achievement without showing that they were clearly frozen goals, ruler-attributable, or durable outcomes across the identified portfolio."}],"overall_assessment":"The answers are generally well-qualified and cite substantial contrary material, but repeatedly conflate formal design, budgets, staffing, institutional activity, and project completion with ruler-attributed effective execution. The main audit defects are over-weighting military and administrative inputs, using 2018-2022 evidence as direct 2023 results, crediting joint or agency-level achievements to López Obrador, and under-integrating the strongest 2023 monitoring evidence on weak results orientation, ignored recommendations, incomplete delivery, and fragile durability."}
